page: Microsoft Azure FX32-16ms_v2 is a memory-intensive virtual machine belonging to the FXmsv2 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor with a high base clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The configuration provides 16 dedicated vCPUs derived from 8 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. Cache resources include 48 KB L1d cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and a large 260 MB L3 cache. It is equipped with 672.0 GB of system memory, yielding an exceptionally high allocation of 42.0 GB of RAM per core. No local storage or GPUs are bundled with this instance, though it is premium storage capable.

In benchmark evaluations, the FX32-16ms_v2 demonstrates strong single-core capabilities. Its Geekbench single-core score of 2336.0 and text processing score of 2948.0 both rank in the top tier. Single-threaded compression and decompression performance are also strong, with gzip compression reaching 34.66 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 14.31 GB/sec. Multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics generally fall within the average range, with uncached memory read bandwidth at 131.99 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 90.97 GB/sec. The processor supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel AMX, which assist in workloads like low-latency LLM inference, where it achieves a strong 289.22 tokens/sec for small model text generation.

From a resource density perspective, the FX32-16ms_v2 offers a highly specialized hardware profile. The extreme memory-to-vCPU ratio makes it a qualitatively cost-effective choice for memory-bound workloads that do not require massive parallel CPU scaling, allowing organizations to avoid paying for excess vCPUs just to acquire large memory footprints. The lack of local storage requires external premium storage attachment, which is a key architectural tradeoff to consider. This server is best suited for large in-memory databases, heavy caching layers, enterprise resource planning systems, and memory-intensive data processing tasks.
